status_summary: One element is operative, two are proposed and one is related. The FCC's Second Report and Order speeding initial processing of satellite and earth station applications was published 2025-08-27 and took effect 2025-09-26 for most provisions. A broader satellite licensing overhaul (Space Modernization for the 21st Century) was proposed 2025-12-05, and the notice for the FCC's 2026-07-22 meeting lists a Report and Order for it that would replace Part 25 with a new Part 100; its adoption was not confirmed, and no final rule had been published in the Federal Register as of 2026-10-07. On wireline deployment, a proposal adopted 2026-06-25 and published 2026-08-07 (WC Docket 25-253) would set a 120-day deadline for state and local right-of-way decisions and limit fees to a reasonable approximation of actual direct costs; comments were due 2026-09-21 and replies are due 2026-11-05. It addresses state and local governments, and the part read does not address federal lands. For federal lands, Interior's regulatory agenda published 2026-08-14 lists a rule on broadband and rights-of-way under 43 CFR 2800 with no scope stated, and no directive to the Bureau of Land Management or Forest Service on review timeliness was found. On funding, NTIA told a House subcommittee on 2026-06-30 that it had approved 54 of 56 BEAD final proposals under the Benefit of the Bargain reforms, which removed a fiber preference, and that about $21 billion in savings was expected, with guidance on using the savings due that summer. That is a cost and technology reform of a program aimed at unserved locations, not the chapter's call to stop funding overbuilding of existing networks, and the chapter's example of Treasury's 2022 American Rescue Plan rules was not researched.

timeline.event: FCC Second Report and Order on expediting initial processing of satellite and earth station applications is published as a final rule (removes some license modification filings and outdated rules).
FCC proposed rule, Space Modernization for the 21st Century, would overhaul space and earth station licensing through a licensing assembly line to speed reviews.

Advisory Council on Historic Preservation publishes amendments extending the Broadband Program Comment, which spares listed agencies duplicative Section 106 reviews of wireless facilities already reviewed by the FCC, to 2030-09-30 and adding the Department of Veterans Affairs.

NTIA's Administrator tells a House subcommittee that 54 of 56 BEAD final proposals are approved, that the reforms are expected to save about $21 billion, and that guidance on nondeployment funds is expected that summer.
FCC Sunshine Act notice lists a Report and Order and further notice on Space Modernization (replacing Part 25 with a new Part 100) for the 2026-07-22 meeting; adoption is not confirmed here.

FCC proposed rule, Build America: Eliminating Barriers to Wireline Deployments, would set a 120-day shot clock and cost-based fee limits with safe harbors for state and local right-of-way approvals (adopted 2026-06-25; comments due 2026-09-21, replies 2026-11-05).
Interior's regulatory agenda lists a rule on broadband and rights-of-way under 43 CFR 2800 (RIN 1004-AF32); only the title appears in the excerpt read.

title: Streamline broadband infrastructure permitting and speed satellite licensing
uncertainties: Whether the Space Modernization order was adopted on 2026-07-22 and when it will be published is unknown; the Sunshine notice describes the item in future terms and the Federal Register showed no final rule as of 2026-10-07. The wireline proposal was read only to character 100,000 of about 141,000, so a federal-lands provision cannot be ruled out. The Interior agenda item is known by title only. The BEAD figures come from a trade summary of congressional testimony, not NTIA's own documents, and the guidance on nondeployment funds was not confirmed as issued. Treasury's 2022 ARPA rules and any change to them were not researched. No directive from the White House or Interior on timely federal-land broadband reviews was found in the searches run (Federal Register terms on broadband and federal lands).
